messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1 — Atlas Telecom (dedicated pool ap-southeast1) p99 latency spike. Current p99 2.8s (SLO 2.0s). Error rate nominal. Page sent to #oncall-sre at 11:03 UTC.

Max Chen: I'm on it, pulling dashboards. @Priya can you ack and start triage?

Priya Rao: acked. seeing the spike correlated with a traffic surge from tenant atlas-prod-ctn. p95 ~420ms, p99 ~2.8s. throughput up ~3x last 10m.

Luis Ortega: copying measurements from infra trace:
```
cluster: rw-dedicated-apse1-pool-7
metric: inference.p99_latency
last_5m: 2.8s
cpu_util: 92%
gpu_util: 98%
queue_depth: 330
prefix_cache_hit: 65%
```

Aisha - Support: Jules (Atlas) just posted to their ops channel, they're seeing customer-facing timeouts on chat flows. They want ETA. Jules says >5% of requests hit >1.5s on their critical route.

Jules (Atlas Ops): confirmed — affecting ~12% of sessions intermittently. They have a customer meeting in 25m. Need mitigation plan asap.

Max Chen: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) add capacity to pool (scale up GPUs), 2) isolate top-consuming tenant (evict or throttle atlas-prod-ctn), 3) failover traffic to warm spare region (ap-southeast2), 4) downgrade model variant to smaller quantized profile for that tenant. Which to pick first?

Priya Rao: scaling is fastest. I'll run the autoscale override to add 3 instances to pool while we decide on isolation.

Nate (eng-sre): queue flood looks like KV lookups plus long sequences from that tenant. Suggests enabling aggressive caching + shorter max seq for their route as a temporary config. I can flip the route config if we get signoff.

Luis Ortega: starting capacity add now:
```
# scale command (internal)
rwctl pool scale --pool rw-dedicated-apse1-pool-7 --add 3
```

deploy-bot: Deployment event queued: pool-scaler-job-3805120987 started. ETA ~ 2m.

Priya Rao: scaling confirmed, new instances initializing. Watching p99.

(2m pass)

Priya Rao: scaling helped but p99 still at 2.1s — improved from 2.8s but not under 2.0. Atlas traffic still heavy.

Max Chen: ok prepare tenant isolation play: reduce max concurrency for atlas-prod-ctn to 1.0 RPS per replica and enable soft-queue. This should limit their tail while keeping service alive. @Jules we'll notify them about throttling window.

Jules (Atlas Ops): do it. They prefer throttling vs full eviction. We'll send customer comms now.

Nate (eng-sre): applying soft throttle now:
```
rwctl tenant throttle --tenant atlas-prod-ctn --rps 1.0 --soft-queue true --duration 15m --reason "p99 mitigation"
```

Priya Rao: throttle applied. p99 dropped to 1.85s on the dashboards. p95 unchanged.

Jules (Atlas Ops): thanks — customer rep says initial load is settling, they're happy with partial throttle for now. Please note they'll still run a big nightly job in ~2h; would like more permanent solution before that.

Max Chen: follow-ups: 1) investigate root cause of sudden traffic burst (customer side surge vs misbehavior), 2) recommend permanent partitioning for atlas tenant if pattern repeats, 3) post-mortem with atlas. Who owns? @Aisha please coordinate customer comms and request timeline for nightly job.

Aisha - Support: I'll open the incident ticket for Atlas, note mitigation steps and get their schedule. Adding escalation to AM.

Luis Ortega: also recording infra anomalies: two nodes showed transient GC stalls during the surge — logs: `gpu-unavailable` events 11:01–11:04 on node-7b3. I pulled logs to /internal/incident/3805120987/logs.

Priya Rao: GC stalls + full GPU at 98% suggests we should review model batching behavior for that tenant. For the short term, throttle + scale worked.

Max Chen: propose we keep throttle in place for 30m total and schedule controlled rollback after we confirm p99 stability. If p99 creeps up again, plan B is warm-spare failover for a subset of atlas traffic. Agreed?

Nate (eng-sre): agreed. I'll set an alert to auto-escalate if p99 > 2.0s for 3 consecutive 1m windows.

deploy-bot: pool-scaler-job-3805120987 completed successfully. Added 3 instances.

(10m later)

Priya Rao: p99 1.6s, queue depth down to 70, GPU utilization ~78%. Removing autoscale override after steady state.

Nate (eng-sre): keeping throttle until handoff to next oncall at 11:40 UTC. I'll add playbook notes to the incident ticket.

Aisha - Support: Customer update sent: summarized actions (scale, throttle), ETA for next update 20m, offered to move their nightly job if needed. Jules confirmed they will try to postpone heavy batch.

Max Chen: thanks all. Handoff: @Nate you are taking next 2h watch and will escalate to infra if p99 regresses. I'll start the post-incident timeline draft.

Nate (eng-sre): taking watch. I'll annotate the runbook with commands used and timeline.

Jules (Atlas Ops): appreciate the fast response team. Please keep me in thread for any rollback or further throttle adjustments.

incident-bot: Incident P1 (3805120987) status -> mitigated (partial). Runbook link: https://internal.rw/incidents/3805120987 — owners: Max Chen, Nate (eng-sre), Aisha - Support.

Max Chen: closing warboard for now. We'll reconvene if auto-escalation triggers. :thumbsup:
